tools.name: set_color_scheme
tools.description: Set light/dark/auto color scheme and optional edit target.

tools.description: Capture the current rendered state of the theme preview as an image: exactly what the user sees. Returns one JPEG per visible preview frame (two when a compare mode is active, labeled e.g. Light/Dark). Call after applying a batch of theme changes to verify the visual result, especially when matching a reference image.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Search the product catalog by free-text query (e.g. 'waterproof trail shoe', 'blue running', 'jacket'). Returns matching products with SKU, title, brand, color, price, imageUrl, and imageAlt.

query.description: Free-text search query.

tools.name: view_product
tools.description: Look at one product in detail by SKU (from search_products results). Highlights it on the page and returns its full description plus imageUrl/imageAlt. Read-only.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a product to the shopper's cart by SKU (from search_products results). Returns the updated cart so you can confirm the running total.

tools.name: remove_from_cart
tools.description: Remove a product from the cart by SKU, or reduce its quantity. Omit quantity to remove the line entirely. Returns the updated cart.

tools.name: apply_promo
tools.description: Apply a promo code to the cart (e.g. TRAIL10, TRAILVIP, SUMMIT20). Returns whether it was accepted and the updated cart with the discount applied.

tools.name: get_calendar_state
tools.description: Read the current calendar state: current local date-time, selected date, visible week, timezone, total event count, visible events, and the valid users (with the userIds create_event accepts). Call this before creating or editing events. All event times are local wall-clock times in the calendar timezone.

tools.name: get_events
tools.description: List calendar events. Optionally filter by month in YYYY-MM format, userId, or a text search over title/description/location.

tools.name: find_availability
tools.description: Find open slots on a date, optionally for a single user. Workday is 9am-5pm local time. Returned slot times are local wall-clock times in the calendar timezone.

tools.name: select_date
tools.description: Move the calendar UI to a specific date without creating an event.

tools.name: create_event
tools.description: Create a calendar event and render it on the page. startDate/endDate are LOCAL wall-clock times in the calendar timezone, formatted YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm: never append "Z" or a UTC offset (any offset is ignored and the stated clock time is used as-is). Use a userId from get_calendar_state.

startDate.description: Event start as local wall-clock time, e.g. 2026-06-11T08:00. No "Z" or UTC offset.

endDate.description: Event end as local wall-clock time, e.g. 2026-06-11T09:00. No "Z" or UTC offset.

tools.name: update_event
tools.description: Update an existing event by eventId. Only supplied fields are changed. startDate/endDate are LOCAL wall-clock times (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm, no "Z" or UTC offset).

startDate.description: Local wall-clock time, e.g. 2026-06-11T08:00. No "Z" or UTC offset.

endDate.description: Local wall-clock time, e.g. 2026-06-11T09:00. No "Z" or UTC offset.

tools.name: delete_event
tools.description: Delete an event from the calendar by eventId.

tools.name: get_deck_overview
tools.description: Read the deck: title, active theme, slide count, and per-slide {id, position, title, elementCount}. Call this first to orient yourself; positions are 1-based.

tools.name: get_slide
tools.description: Read one slide's full contents: every element with its id, geometry, and style. Call this before editing a slide's elements. Defaults to the slide open in the editor.

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: Read the elements the user currently has selected on the canvas: ids, types, geometry, and styles. Use this whenever the user says 'this', 'these', or refers to something they clicked.

tools.name: list_themes
tools.description: List the available deck themes with their palettes and fonts.

tools.name: goto_slide
tools.description: Open a slide in the editor (navigation only: changes nothing).

tools.name: add_slide
tools.description: Insert a new slide from a layout. 'title' = centered title + subtitle; 'title-body' = heading + body text; 'two-col' = heading + two text columns (body fills the left, right starts empty); 'blank' = empty. Returns the new slide id and its element ids so you can refine them with update_element.

body.description: Body text. Use \n for line breaks, • for bullets.

position.description: 1-based position to insert at; defaults to the end of the deck.

tools.name: duplicate_slide
tools.description: Copy a slide (and all its elements) right after the original. Returns the new slide id.

position.description: 1-based position of the slide to copy.

tools.name: delete_slide
tools.description: Permanently remove a slide and all its elements.

tools.name: reorder_slides
tools.description: Move a slide to a new 1-based position. Returns the resulting slide order.

tools.name: set_slide_props
tools.description: Update a slide's title and/or background color.

background.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

tools.name: add_element
tools.description: Add one element (text box, rectangle, ellipse, line, or image) to a slide. Lines draw from the top-left to the bottom-right corner of their bounding box. Returns the new element id.

slideId.description: Target slide id; defaults to the slide open in the editor.

x.description: Slide units; the canvas is 960 wide x 540 tall, origin at the top-left.

z.description: Stacking order; higher renders on top.

text.description: Text elements only. Use \n for line breaks.

fontFamily.description: Font stack, or a theme token: 'theme.heading' / 'theme.body'. Prefer tokens.

color.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

fill.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

stroke.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

src.description: Image URL, or 'placeholder' for a styled placeholder block.

tools.name: update_element
tools.description: Merge a partial patch into one element: position, size, text, and style in a single call. Omitted keys are unchanged. Returns the updated element.

patch.description: Partial element properties to merge; omitted keys are unchanged.

x.description: Slide units; the canvas is 960 wide x 540 tall, origin at the top-left.

z.description: Stacking order; higher renders on top.

text.description: Text elements only. Use \n for line breaks.

fontFamily.description: Font stack, or a theme token: 'theme.heading' / 'theme.body'. Prefer tokens.

color.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

fill.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

stroke.description: CSS color (e.g. '#0f172a') or a theme token: 'theme.background', 'theme.surface', 'theme.text', 'theme.accent', 'theme.accentText'. Prefer tokens so the deck restyles when the theme changes.

src.description: Image URL, or 'placeholder' for a styled placeholder block.

tools.name: delete_elements
tools.description: Permanently remove one or more elements by id.

tools.name: align_elements
tools.description: Align elements to the slide or to their shared bounding box, and/or space them evenly along an axis (distribute needs 3+ elements; the first/last stay put). Same shape as align_selection. Returns the new positions.

distribute.description: Space the elements evenly along this axis; needs 3+ elements.

relativeTo.description: Default 'slide'. 'selection-bounds' aligns within the group's own bounding box.

tools.name: set_deck_title
tools.description: Set the deck's title.

tools.name: apply_theme
tools.description: Switch the deck's theme. Every element using theme tokens ('theme.accent', 'theme.heading', …) restyles across ALL slides.

tools.name: enter_presenter_mode
tools.description: Enter full-screen presenter mode. NOTE: this replaces your editing tools with presentation controls (next_slide, prev_slide, jump_to_slide, exit_presenter_mode) until the show ends.

position.description: 1-based slide to start from; defaults to slide 1.

url.description: Image URL (absolute, or relative to the current page) to fetch and inspect.

For shipment delivery addresses: ALWAYS first call shipment-tracker Filter (when criteria given) and then shipment-tracker GetData to fetch the current rows. Each grid row exposes DestinationStreet, Destination (city), DestinationLat and DestinationLng — pass DestinationLat as latitude and DestinationLng as longitude, one call per shipment. Use DestinationStreet or '{TrackingNumber} — {Destination}' as the marker title. Available warehouses (for warehouse pins): Chicago Hub (Chicago, USA, North America) at [41.88, -87.63], capacity 78%; Rotterdam Port (Rotterdam, Netherlands, Europe) at [51.92, 4.48], capacity 85%; Shanghai Terminal (Shanghai, China, Asia Pacific) at [31.23, 121.47], capacity 92%; São Paulo Center (São Paulo, Brazil, Latin America) at [-23.55, -46.63], capacity 61%; Mumbai Gateway (Mumbai, India, Asia Pacific) at [19.08, 72.88], capacity 88%; Tokyo Depot (Tokyo, Japan, Asia Pacific) at [35.68, 139.69], capacity 73%; Sydney Warehouse (Sydney, Australia, Oceania) at [-33.87, 151.21], capacity 55%; Lagos Depot (Lagos, Nigeria, Africa) at [6.52, 3.38], capacity 42% (warehouse-map map)

tools.name: inventory-sheet-spreadsheet-set-cell
tools.description: Write a single cell value into the Warehouse Capacity spreadsheet. To populate the spreadsheet from the Shipment Tracker grid, ALWAYS first call shipment-tracker Filter (if criteria given) and then shipment-tracker GetData to retrieve the visible rows. Then call this tool MULTIPLE TIMES to write: (1) a header row at row 1 with columns A='Tracking #', B='Origin', C='Destination', D='Delivery Address', E='Status', F='Carrier', G='Value', H='Weight (kg)', I='Ship Date', J='ETA', K='Dest. Lat', L='Dest. Lng'; and (2) one row per shipment starting at row 2, mapping TrackingNumber→A, Origin→B, Destination→C, DestinationStreet→D, Status→E, Carrier→F, Value→G, Weight→H, ShipDate→I, ETA→J, DestinationLat→K, DestinationLng→L. Cell addresses use A1 notation (e.g. 'A1', 'B2'). Clear any old rows the user no longer wants before writing new ones. (inventory-sheet spreadsheet)

name.description: The skill name (case-insensitive). Either id or name must be provided.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Reads the complete current editor content.

tools.name: read_selection
tools.description: Reads the currently selected text in the editor.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Finds all occurrences of a query string in the document. Returns the line and column of each match.

query.description: The text to search for.

tools.name: get_metadata
tools.description: Returns metadata about the current document: character count, word count, and line count.

tools.name: get_current_mode
tools.description: Returns the current UI mode: 'editor' (Monaco editor is visible) or 'preview' (Markdown preview is visible). Check this before making edits to ensure the editor is accessible.

tools.name: request_switch_to_editor
tools.description: Requests the user to switch from Preview mode to Editor mode. This will display a prompt to the user and pause until they accept or decline. Call this before attempting edits when in preview mode.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Proposes a targeted edit. This tool pauses and waits for user approval. ONLY use this for small, localized changes (e.g., 1-2 sentences). Never pass the entire document.

originalText.description: The exact, minimal string of text to replace. Must be short. Do NOT pass the whole document.

replacementText.description: The new text to replace the originalText with.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Proposes a complete rewrite. This tool pauses and waits for user approval. ONLY use this when the user explicitly requests a total rewrite of the entire document.

tools.name: get_active_doc_info
tools.description: Returns the id and title of the document currently open in the editor.

tools.name: list_workspace_docs
tools.description: Lists all documents in the workspace. Returns an array of { id, title } objects.

tools.description: Reads the full content of a specific document. Returns { title, content } or { error }.

id.description: The document ID to read.

tools.description: Asks a question about a specific document using a sub-agent. Returns { summary, excerpt } where excerpt is the most relevant verbatim passage.

id.description: The document ID to query.

query.description: The question about the document.

tools.name: query_workspace
tools.description: Asks a question spanning all workspace documents and synthesizes the results. Returns { summary, sources: [{ id, title, excerpt }] }.

query.description: The question to answer across all documents.

tools.name: create_document
tools.description: Creates a new document in the workspace with the given title and optional initial content. Providing content avoids a separate write step. Pauses for user authorization before creating.

title.description: The title for the new document.

content.description: Optional initial content for the new document. If omitted the document is created blank.

tools.name: rename_document
tools.description: Renames an existing document in the workspace. Pauses for user authorization before renaming.

id.description: The document ID to rename.

title.description: The new title for the document.

tools.name: delete_document
tools.description: Deletes a document from the workspace. Pauses for user authorization before deleting. If the deleted document was active, a different document becomes active.

id.description: The document ID to delete.

tools.name: switch_active_document
tools.description: Switches the active document in the editor. Saves the current document content before switching. Does not require user authorization.

id.description: The document ID to switch to.

tools.description: Translate a piece of text from one language to another using an on-device AI model. Languages are specified as BCP 47 tags (e.g. 'en', 'fr', 'ja').

sourceLanguage.description: BCP 47 language tag of the source language (e.g. "en").

targetLanguage.description: BCP 47 language tag of the target language (e.g. "fr").

tools.name: delegate_to_skill
tools.description: Delegates a task to a named skill (sub-agent). The skill runs with read-only access and returns its response as a string. Interpret the response and act on it accordingly.

skillName.description: The exact name of the skill to invoke.

task.description: The specific task or instructions to pass to the skill.

tools.name: invoke_agent
tools.description: Delegates an ad-hoc task to a generic sub-agent. The sub-agent runs with the given system prompt and optional tool groups. Returns { result: string } with the sub-agent's final response.

systemPrompt.description: The system prompt / instructions for the sub-agent.

task.description: The task or question to send to the sub-agent.

tools.description: Optional tool group names to give the sub-agent. Supported: 'workspace_readonly'.

tools.name: invoke_planner
tools.description: Decomposes a high-level task into a structured step-by-step Plan. Returns a JSON string: { goal, steps: [{ id, instruction, dependsOn }] }. The Orchestrator reads the plan and dispatches each step using the appropriate tools.

task.description: The high-level task to decompose into a plan.

context.description: Optional additional context (e.g. current document summary, workspace doc list).

tools.name: invoke_researcher
tools.description: Queries workspace documents and synthesizes a structured answer. Returns JSON: { summary, sources: [{ id, title, excerpt }] }. Use this when the task requires finding information across workspace documents before writing or reviewing.

query.description: The question or information need to research.

docIds.description: Optional list of document IDs to restrict the search to. If omitted, all workspace documents are queried.

tools.name: invoke_writer
tools.description: Generates draft text for a single targeted section from an instruction and optional research/style context. Returns { draft: string } — raw text only, no edits applied. After receiving the draft, apply it using edit() for the target section. Do NOT use this to rewrite the whole document at once — use invoke_planner to break full-document tasks into per-section steps.

instruction.description: What to write. Be explicit: specify the target section, desired length, and any constraints.

researchContext.description: JSON-encoded ResearchResult from invoke_researcher. Inject when the draft should cite workspace sources.

styleContext.description: A verbatim excerpt from the document the Writer should match in tone, voice, and formatting.

tools.name: invoke_reviewer
tools.description: Evaluates a draft against explicit criteria and returns structured feedback. Returns JSON: { passed: boolean, issues: [{ severity, location?, description, fix? }], summary }. Use after invoke_writer to check a draft before applying it. If passed is false and error-severity issues remain after 3 Writer→Reviewer cycles, present the best available draft via edit() or write() and summarise remaining issues in your response.

criteria.description: Review criteria to check against (e.g. 'grammatical correctness', 'consistent use of past tense', 'no unsupported factual claims').

tools.name: add_sauce
tools.description: Append one sauce stripe. Use green_liquid, mustard, chocolate_syrup, or pink_frosting.

tools.name: set_garnish
tools.description: Set the final garnish. Use none, tiny_umbrella, birthday_candle, bacon_strip, or eyeball_toothpick.

tools.name: plate_it
tools.description: Choose the serving vessel and reveal the chef verdict. Use plate, paper_boat, cutting_board, or pan.

sites.name: fieldwork-beat-machine.openai.chatgpt.site
sites.description: A tactile 12-voice beat machine with classic drum-machine grooves, deep synths, keyboard and touch pads, WebMCP controls, and stereo WAV export.

tools.name: get_state
tools.description: Read the current beat-machine preset, tempo, transport, musical key and scale, 24-sound library, six editable instrument slots and their complete sound-design parameters, selected pad bank, all 12 playable pads, plus the 12 by 16 velocity and MIDI-note patterns.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Read the complete portable Fieldwork project document, including its name, pattern, notes, mix, musical key, and six instrument patches. Use it for backup or as input to load_project.

tools.name: load_project
tools.description: Validate and atomically replace the current local project with a Fieldwork project document. Stops playback and recording, preserves an undo step, and autosaves locally. Invalid documents leave the current project unchanged.

tools.name: export_project
tools.description: Create a portable JSON backup of the current project and optionally download it. This does not render audio; use export_track for WAV audio.

tools.name: undo_edit
tools.description: Undo the most recent local project edit. Returns changed=false when no undo history remains.

tools.name: redo_edit
tools.description: Restore the most recently undone local project edit. Returns changed=false when no redo history remains.

tools.name: set_tempo
tools.description: Set the beat-machine tempo in BPM (45 to 220).

tools.name: set_swing
tools.description: Set sixteenth-note swing. Use a fraction from 0 to 0.45 or a percentage from 0 to 45.

tools.name: set_controls
tools.description: Adjust the beat-machine mix and timing controls: tempo, swing, tone, space, master volume, humanize, and default export bars. Omitted controls stay unchanged.

tools.name: select_kit
tools.description: Load one of the nine instrument and groove presets: 808-night, 909-warehouse, linn-pop, sp-dust, mpc-swing, acid-cell, electro-break, dub-orbit, or minimal-12.

tools.name: select_instrument
tools.description: Map the performance pads to all voices, a 12-pad drum bank, or one of six playable instrument slots using the selected key and scale. Slots are laid out U I O / J K L; instruments can be lead, chord, pluck, bass, sub, or tuned fx.

tools.name: configure_instrument
tools.description: Load one of 24 categorized sound presets into a U I O / J K L instrument slot, or target a base voice. Sounds cover neon leads, pads, brass, strings, keys, bells, acid, reese, 808 and sub basses, noise, radio, and atmospheric FX.

tools.name: configure_instruments
tools.description: Atomically load sounds into 1 to 6 distinct U I O / J K L instrument slots. Results preserve input order; duplicate slots or any invalid item reject the whole batch without changing the current configuration.

tools.name: set_instrument_params
tools.description: Dial in an instrument slot with attack, decay, sustain, release, cutoff, resonance, drive, motion, stereo width, octave, and waveform. Omitted sound-design controls stay unchanged and changes apply to live playback and WAV export.

tools.name: reset_instrument
tools.description: Restore a U I O / J K L instrument slot's current sound preset to its original ADSR, filter, drive, motion, width, octave, and waveform settings.

tools.name: randomize_instrument
tools.description: Create a playable sound-design variation for a U I O / J K L instrument slot. An optional seed makes the ADSR, filter, motion, waveform, and timbre result repeatable.

tools.name: set_key
tools.description: Choose the musical root and scale used by all twelve melodic pads. Root accepts note names such as C, F#, Bb, or a pitch class from 0 to 11; scales are minor, major, dorian, pentatonic, and chromatic.

tools.name: set_step
tools.description: Write or clear a single sequencer step, optionally setting a MIDI note for a melodic lane. Steps are numbered 1 to 16; voices include kick, snare, clap, hatClosed, hatOpen, perc, sub, bass, chord, lead, pluck, and fx.

tools.name: set_pattern
tools.description: Replace any number of voice lanes in the 16-step sequencer. Supply velocity lanes and, optionally, matching MIDI-note lanes to lay complete melodic tracks in one action; omitted lanes stay unchanged.

tools.name: clear_pattern
tools.description: Clear all 12 sequencer lanes, leaving a silent 16-step grid ready for an agent or performer to lay a new track.

tools.name: set_voice_mute
tools.description: Mute or unmute one instrument lane without deleting its sequencer steps.

tools.name: set_recording
tools.description: Arm or disarm on-tempo grid recording. When armed, performance pads and trigger-pad actions can print at the playhead.

tools.name: mutate_pattern
tools.description: Create a musical variation or fill while keeping the core kick and sub pocket intact.

tools.name: transport
tools.description: Start, stop, or toggle the beat-machine transport.

tools.name: trigger_pad
tools.description: Audition a voice or one of the 12 currently mapped performance pads and optionally place it onto the current sequencer step. Melodic pads automatically print their note; an explicit MIDI note can override it.

tools.name: export_track
tools.description: Render the current beat and synth arrangement to a stereo 48 kHz WAV file, make it available for preview, and optionally download it.

sites.name: admintoolkit.io
sites.description: admintoolkit.io gives admins browser-based DNS, mail authentication, TLS, HTTP, public IP, CIDR, and EDID checks with local parsing and explicit live lookups.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_ai_crawler_access
tools.description: Return a read-only RFC 9309 robots.txt access report for AI and search crawlers. Accepts robots.txt text or a public robots.txt URL plus an optional path. Includes merged matching groups, octet-normalized longest-match decisions, per-crawler evidence, transport status, crawler-registry provenance and policy snippets.

content.description: Pasted robots.txt content to validate locally, e.g. 'User-agent: GPTBot'.

crawlers.description: Crawler tokens to evaluate as an array, e.g. ['GPTBot','Google-Extended'].

path.description: Path to evaluate against robots.txt rules, e.g. '/' or '/tools/'.

url.description: Robots.txt URL or bare domain to fetch, e.g. 'https://example.com/robots.txt'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_validate_llms_txt
tools.description: Validate the required initial H1, optional summary and project details, and any H2 resource lists with link titles, URLs, optional descriptions, findings, and source-line evidence.

content.description: Pasted llms.txt Markdown content to validate locally, e.g. '# Example'.

url.description: llms.txt URL or bare domain to fetch, e.g. 'https://example.com/llms.txt'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_validate_a2a_agent_card
tools.description: Return a read-only version-aware A2A Agent Card validation report. Includes v0.2, v0.3 and v1.0 structure plus discovery-path evidence without claiming endpoint, authentication or signature conformance.

json.description: Pasted Agent Card JSON to validate locally, e.g. '{"name":"Agent"}'.

url.description: Agent Card URL or bare domain to fetch, e.g. 'https://example.com/.well-known/agent-card.json'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_validate_webmcp_tool
tools.description: Return a read-only WebMCP report for pasted or fetched source. Includes declarative and imperative static-source evidence separately from caller-provided runtime observation; pasted JavaScript is never executed and active runtime tools are never inferred from source alone.

source.description: Pasted HTML or JavaScript source to validate locally, e.g. 'data-tool-name=demo'.

url.description: Public page URL to fetch for WebMCP validation, e.g. 'https://example.com/'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_mx_records
tools.description: Return a read-only MX routing report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain name. Includes exchanger hosts, preferences, Null MX, CNAME risk, address resolution and actionable mail-routing warnings.

domain.description: Mail domain to check via DNS MX lookup, e.g. 'example.com'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_email_auth_records
tools.description: Return a read-only SPF, DMARC and DKIM report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain plus optional pasted TXT values. Includes syntax, policy strength, alignment, DNS evidence and record-specific warnings.

dkim_record.description: Pasted DKIM TXT value, e.g. 'v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=...'.

dmarc_record.description: Pasted DMARC TXT record, e.g. 'v=DMARC1; p=reject'.

domain.description: Mail domain to check, e.g. 'example.com'.

selector.description: DKIM selector to query, e.g. 's1' or 'default'.

spf_record.description: Pasted SPF TXT record, e.g. 'v=spf1 redirect=spf.example.com'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_analyze_email_headers
tools.description: Return a read-only email message header report. Accepts pasted RFC 5322 headers. Includes raw Received order, recorded Authentication-Results and caller-configured authserv-id trust; it does not perform cryptographic authentication or reverse-DNS verification.

headers.description: Full email headers to analyze, e.g. 'Authentication-Results: ...'.

trusted_authserv_ids.description: Optional authserv-id values explicitly trusted by the caller; without them, Authentication-Results remain unverified recorded claims.

tools.name: admintoolkit_validate_arc_chain
tools.description: Return a read-only ARC structural validation report. Accepts pasted ARC-Seal, ARC-Message-Signature and ARC-Authentication-Results fields. Includes structural completeness, instance continuity and recorded cv state; cryptographic validation and sealer trust are not evaluated.

headers.description: Message headers containing ARC fields, e.g. 'ARC-Seal: i=1; ...'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_bimi_record
tools.description: Return a read-only BIMI readiness report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain, selector and optional BIMI, DMARC, logo or certificate evidence. Includes TXT syntax, DMARC dependency, asset URL findings and a conservative BIMI draft.

dmarc.description: Pasted DMARC TXT record for BIMI policy review, e.g. 'v=DMARC1; p=reject'.

domain.description: BIMI domain to check, e.g. 'example.com'.

evidence_url.description: BIMI VMC or evidence URL to inspect, e.g. 'https://example.com/vmc.pem'.

logo_url.description: BIMI SVG logo URL to inspect, e.g. 'https://example.com/logo.svg'.

record.description: Pasted BIMI TXT record, e.g. 'v=BIMI1; l=https://example.com/logo.svg'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_mta_sts_policy
tools.description: Return a read-only MTA-STS deployment report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain plus optional TXT, policy, MX and TLS-RPT evidence. Includes mode, max-age, syntax, id consistency, MX coverage, conformance findings and remediation warnings.

domain.description: Mail domain for MTA-STS checks, e.g. 'example.com'.

mode.description: Generated MTA-STS policy mode: 'testing', 'enforce', or 'none', e.g. 'testing'.

mx_hosts.description: Known MX hostnames, one per line, e.g. 'mail.example.com'.

policy.description: Pasted MTA-STS policy text, e.g. 'version: STSv1'.

tls_rpt.description: Pasted TLS-RPT TXT value, e.g. 'v=TLSRPTv1; rua=mailto:tls@example.com'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_tls_rpt_policy
tools.description: Return a read-only SMTP TLS Reporting report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain plus optional TLS-RPT TXT or RUA values. Includes version syntax, reporting destinations, external-provider use, conformance findings and remediation warnings.

domain.description: Mail domain for TLS-RPT checks, e.g. 'example.com'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_smtp_tls_readiness
tools.description: Return a read-only SMTP TLS delivery readiness report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain and optional MTA-STS, TLS-RPT, DANE and FCrDNS checks. Includes MX, STARTTLS, certificate, policy-alignment and downgrade-risk findings.

check_dane.description: Include DANE/TLSA checks; pass true or false, e.g. true.

check_fcrdns.description: Include forward-confirmed reverse DNS checks; pass true or false, e.g. true.

check_mta_sts.description: Include MTA-STS checks; pass true or false, e.g. true.

check_tls_rpt.description: Include TLS-RPT checks; pass true or false, e.g. true.

domain.description: Mail domain for SMTP TLS readiness checks, e.g. 'example.com'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_validate_dnssec_records
tools.description: Return a read-only DNSSEC evidence report for a domain. Accepts a domain plus optional DS, DNSKEY, RRSIG and resolver-status data. Includes chain readiness, algorithms, missing records, validation findings and warnings.

dnskey_records.description: DNSKEY records for the zone, one per line, e.g. '257 3 13 <key>'.

domain.description: DNSSEC domain to validate, e.g. 'example.com'.

ds_records.description: DS records for the domain, one per line, e.g. '12345 13 2 <digest>'.

rrsig_records.description: RRSIG records for validation context, one per line, e.g. 'example.com. RRSIG ...'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_generate_tlsa_record
tools.description: Return a read-only DANE TLSA record report. Accepts host, port, protocol, usage, selector, matching type and optional certificate data. Includes owner name, digest, generated TLSA data and DNS comparison findings.

file.description: Certificate file content to parse, e.g. PEM text from a .crt file.

host.description: TLS service host for TLSA generation, e.g. 'mail.example.com'.

pem.description: Certificate PEM, DER base64, or hex input, e.g. '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----'.

port.description: TLS service port number, e.g. '25' or '443'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_validate_dane_records
tools.description: Return a read-only DANE service validation report. Accepts service host, port, protocol, TLSA records, DNSSEC status and optional certificate evidence. Includes owner names, TLSA syntax, DNSSEC dependency and certificate-match findings.

host.description: DANE service host to validate, e.g. 'mail.example.com'.

port.description: DANE service port number, e.g. '25' or '443'.

tlsa_records.description: TLSA records to validate, one per line, e.g. '3 1 1 <sha256>'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_caa_records
tools.description: Return a read-only CAA certificate-authority policy report for a domain. Accepts a domain plus optional CAA records and issuer details. Includes issue, issuewild, iodef, ACME parameters, policy gaps and record-generation guidance.

ca.description: CA domain for generated CAA records, e.g. 'letsencrypt.org'.

domain.description: CAA domain to check, e.g. 'example.com' (no scheme).

issuemail.description: CAA issuemail issuer-domain value from RFC 9495, optionally followed by issuer parameters, e.g. 'letsencrypt.org; validationmethods=dns-01'.

records.description: CAA records to inspect, one per line, e.g. '0 issue letsencrypt.org'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_analyze_http_headers
tools.description: Return a read-only HTTP response-header report for a public endpoint. Accepts pasted headers or a public URL. Includes security, cache, framing, duplicate/conflicting header fields, prioritized findings and remediation notes.

headers.description: Pasted HTTP response headers, e.g. 'Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000'.

url.description: Public URL to fetch for HTTP header analysis, e.g. 'https://example.com/'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_decode_ssl_certificate
tools.description: Return a read-only X.509 TLS certificate report. Accepts PEM text or public TLS host details. Includes subject, issuer, SANs, validity, fingerprints, key usage, extensions, hostname and certificate-health findings.

host.description: TLS certificate host to connect to, e.g. 'example.com'.

pem.description: Certificate PEM text to decode, e.g. '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_validate_security_txt
tools.description: Return a read-only RFC 9116 security.txt report. Accepts pasted content or a public security.txt URL plus optional contact fields. Includes contact, expiry, canonical, encryption, policy, language fields, findings and draft output.

url.description: Public security.txt URL or bare domain, e.g. 'https://example.com/.well-known/security.txt'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_tls_configuration
tools.description: Return a read-only public TLS configuration report for a host. Accepts host and port plus optional HSTS evidence. Includes separate exact-version probes, a distinct verified default handshake, SAN identity/trust evidence, negotiated cipher and ALPN evidence, and HTTPS-only HSTS checks; it does not claim cipher or ALPN enumeration.

host.description: Public TLS DNS host or IP literal to check, e.g. 'example.com' or '1.1.1.1' (no scheme; private/reserved targets are rejected).

hsts.description: Optional pasted HSTS header, e.g. 'max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains'.

port.description: TLS port number to check, e.g. '443'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_redirect_indexability
tools.description: Return a read-only redirect, canonical and indexability report for a public URL. Accepts a URL. Includes bounded per-hop status and SSRF evidence, final URL, HTML and HTTP canonical hints, robots meta and scoped X-Robots-Tag directives, hreflang, separate sitemap reachability and membership, and evidence completeness.

url.description: Public URL to check for redirects and indexability, e.g. 'https://example.com/'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_show_public_ip_context
tools.description: Return a read-only same-origin IP context report for the current request. Requires no input. Includes the canonical primary address, directly observed peer, trusted-proxy decision, preserved forwarded-header claims and observed address family; one request path does not prove dual-stack capability and no third-party Geo-IP lookup is performed.

tools.name: admintoolkit_calculate_cidr_subnet
tools.description: Return a read-only local IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR report. Accepts a CIDR block plus optional split prefix and address family. Includes exact BigInt-derived boundaries and address counts, RFC 3021 /31 and host-route /32 semantics, no IPv6 broadcast claim, embedded-IPv4 parsing and a capped subnet preview.

target.description: Split target prefix length, e.g. '26' for /26 subnets.

tools.name: admintoolkit_decode_edid_data
tools.description: Return a read-only local EDID 1.3/1.4 and bounded CTA report. Includes identity, checksums, feature-qualified preferred timing, detailed timings, SVD/SAD and speaker data, selected CTA extended blocks, and lossless raw unknown blocks from hex or file content. It does not infer Atmos, DTS:X, dynamic HDR, Dolby Vision, HDR10+, FRL, DSC, VRR, ALLM, or QMS from unimplemented evidence.

file.description: EDID file contents as text or hex, e.g. a 128-byte EDID block.

sites.name: betteroff.finance
sites.description: BetterOff keeps household accounts and financial records current, then shows what changed, what is coming, and what needs attention.

tools.name: search_public_docs
tools.description: Use this when an agent needs to search BetterOff public product, pricing, trust, or calculator documents. Do not use it for customer, household, account, or personalized financial data.

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Use this when an agent needs BetterOff's canonical public pricing facts and assumptions. Do not use it for customer billing or account data.

tools.name: get_feature_details
tools.description: Use this when an agent needs public details about one BetterOff feature from the allow-listed corpus. Do not use it for authenticated product state.

tools.name: list_public_calculators
tools.description: Use this to discover BetterOff's free public calculators before choosing one. Results contain canonical URLs and never access customer data.

tools.name: get_public_calculator_contract
tools.description: Use this before running a calculator to retrieve its exact bounded input schema, output schema, methodology, assumptions, and canonical source.

tools.name: run_public_calculator
tools.description: Use this when an agent needs to run one free public BetterOff calculator with bounded JSON input. Results are educational calculations, not personalized financial advice.

tools.name: compare_public_scenarios
tools.description: Use this when an agent needs to run two inputs through the same free public calculator. Returns both results without ranking or personalized advice.

tools.name: calc_debt_payoff
tools.description: Runs debt payoff projections across multiple debts using avalanche or snowball strategy and extra monthly payment.

tools.name: calc_emergency_fund
tools.description: Calculates emergency fund target from monthly expenses and coverage months, tracks progress, and estimates time-to-goal.

monthlyExpenses.description: Monthly essential expenses — Housing, food, utilities, insurance, debt minimums.

monthlySavingsRate.description: Monthly savings rate — Amount directed toward this goal each month.

variableIncomeBufferMonths.description: Extra variable-income buffer (months) — Optional additional coverage for commissions, contract work, seasonal income, or a single-income household.

insuranceDeductibleReserve.description: Insurance deductible reserve — Optional reserve for the largest likely health, home, or auto deductible not already in monthly expenses.

tools.name: calc_fire
tools.description: Estimates financial independence target from annual expenses, withdrawal rate, current savings, monthly investment, and return assumptions.

annualExpenses.description: Annual expenses — Yearly spending to sustain after retirement.

annualReturnPct.description: Expected annual return (%) — Pre-inflation return on invested assets.

withdrawalRatePct.description: Safe withdrawal rate (%) — Percentage of portfolio withdrawn annually in retirement.

annualFeePct.description: Annual investment fees (%) — Deducted from the assumed return.

annualContributionGrowthPct.description: Annual investment growth (%) — Annual increase in the monthly investment amount.

otherAnnualIncome.description: Other annual retirement income — Pension, Social Security, or work income that reduces expenses funded by the portfolio.

tools.name: calc_paycheck
tools.description: Estimates 2026 take-home pay from salary or hourly wages, pay frequency, filing status, state, W-4 settings, FICA, and pre-tax deductions.

stateRatePct.description: Estimated state rate — Used for states without a dated calculator profile.

retirement401kPct.description: 401(k) contribution — Traditional pre-tax contribution as a percentage of gross pay.

tools.name: calc_net_worth
tools.description: Calculates net worth from asset and debt entries, plus liquid net worth and debt percentage of assets.

asOfDate.description: Snapshot date — Date the overall snapshot represents. Add source and valuation date to each item where available.

tools.name: calc_savings_goal
tools.description: Calculates a savings-goal timeline, required monthly savings, and weekly equivalent from a target, current balance, return, and deadline.

annualFeePct.description: Annual fees (%) — Deducted from the assumed annual return.

targetMonths.description: Target timeline (months) — Used to calculate required monthly contribution.

tools.name: calc_retirement
tools.description: Projects retirement savings from age, contributions, return assumptions, and income target, returns the year-by-year balance at each age, then estimates the gap using a 4% withdrawal assumption.

annualReturnPct.description: Expected annual return (%) — Nominal annual return before inflation.

desiredMonthlyIncome.description: Desired retirement income — Monthly income target in retirement.

annualFeePct.description: Annual investment fees (%) — Deducted from the assumed annual return.

annualContributionGrowthPct.description: Annual contribution growth (%) — Increase applied to monthly contributions after each projection year.

withdrawalRatePct.description: Withdrawal-rate assumption (%) — Planning assumption only; it is not guaranteed to be safe.

otherMonthlyIncome.description: Other monthly retirement income — Expected Social Security, pension, or other income that reduces the amount the portfolio must provide.

tools.name: calc_subscription_cost
tools.description: Normalizes mixed-interval subscriptions into monthly-equivalent costs, ranks by impact, and computes triage savings, category totals, and future-price scenarios.

tools.name: calc_compound_interest
tools.description: Calculates compound interest from principal, monthly contributions, annual return, years, and annual, monthly, weekly, or daily compounding.

annualFeePct.description: Annual fees (%) — Deducted from the assumed annual return.

contributionTiming.description: Contribution timing — Whether each monthly contribution is added before or after that month's growth.

tools.name: calc_dca
tools.description: Compares dollar-cost averaging versus lump-sum investing across market scenarios with configurable cadence and horizon.

totalInvestment.description: Total investment — The same total is invested all at once or divided across the DCA schedule.

horizonYears.description: Horizon (years) — How long DCA takes to invest the full amount.

cadence.description: Contribution cadence — How often the calculator makes an equal DCA purchase.

scenario.description: Market scenario — A simplified price path for comparison, not a market forecast.

startPrice.description: Start price — The price used for the lump-sum purchase and the first DCA purchase.

endPrice.description: End price — The price used to value both strategies at the end.

volatilityPct.description: Illustrative path swing (%) — Controls a deterministic sine-shaped price swing. It is not statistical volatility or a forecast.

cashYieldPct.description: Annual yield on uninvested cash — Yield earned while cash waits for later DCA purchases.

feePerPurchase.description: Fee per purchase — A flat trading fee deducted from every scheduled purchase.

tools.name: calc_investment_return
tools.description: Calculates total return, annualized return (CAGR), and dollar gain from initial investment, final value, years, and dividends.

finalValue.description: Final value — Market value at the end of the holding period.

dividendsReceived.description: Dividends received — Cumulative cash dividends over the holding period.

feesPaid.description: Fees paid — Cumulative fees not already reflected in the ending value.

tools.name: calc_portfolio_allocation
tools.description: Calculates an illustrative portfolio allocation across U.S. stocks, international stocks, bonds, and cash based on years to retirement and risk tolerance.

riskCapacity.description: Capacity to absorb losses — Financial ability to tolerate losses, separate from willingness to take risk. The more conservative of the two governs the illustration.

portfolioValue.description: Portfolio value — Your current invested assets.

tools.name: calc_mortgage
tools.description: Calculates monthly PITI mortgage payment, total interest, total cost, and builds amortization schedule from home price, down payment, rate, and term.

downPaymentPct.description: Down payment (%) — Percentage of home price paid upfront as equity.

annualRatePct.description: Interest rate (%) — Fixed annual note rate before fees.

monthlyHOA.description: Monthly HOA — Monthly homeowners association fee, if applicable.

annualPmiRatePct.description: Annual PMI rate (%) — Applies when the down payment is under 20%; use the rate from a loan estimate when available.

closingCosts.description: Closing costs — Upfront lender and transaction costs, excluding the down payment.

monthlyMaintenance.description: Monthly maintenance reserve — Optional owner-paid maintenance budget; not part of PITI.

extraPrincipalMonthly.description: Extra principal each month — Additional principal payment used to shorten payoff and reduce interest.

tools.name: calc_impermanent_loss
tools.description: Estimates impermanent loss from initial investment and token price multipliers in a 50/50 constant-product AMM.

priceChangeA.description: Token A price multiplier — 1.0 = unchanged, 2.0 = doubled, 0.5 = halved.

priceChangeB.description: Token B price multiplier — 1.0 = unchanged, 2.0 = doubled, 0.5 = halved.

tools.name: calc_inflation
tools.description: Projects purchasing power erosion from a present amount, year horizon, and annual inflation rate percent.

inflationRatePct.description: Annual inflation rate (%) — This calculator assumes the same rate every year.

categoryRates.description: Optional category assumptions — Weighted household categories override the single general rate when supplied.

sites.name: pixly.gg
sites.description: Minecraft server hosting with no subscription — pay for the time your server is online. Java + Bedrock crossplay, 1-click mods, 10 free hours to try, no card.

tools.name: mc_list_servers
tools.description: List every Minecraft server owned by the signed-in user, including id, name, domain, region, status and online players.

tools.name: mc_get_server
tools.description: Get full details for one server by id (status, config, instance size, connection address, players).

serverId.description: The target server id (ULID), as returned by mc_list_servers.

tools.name: mc_create_server
tools.description: Create a new Minecraft server. `region` must be an awsRegion id from mc_list_regions. Per-account server limits and wallet balance are enforced server-side; a 402/403 result means the action was blocked, not that it failed transiently.

tools.name: mc_update_server
tools.description: Update a server's name, instance size, autostart, or world config (MOTD, max players, difficulty, version, mods, etc.). Some fields require a restart to take effect.

serverId.description: The target server id (ULID), as returned by mc_list_servers.

resetWorld.description: Confirms a version downgrade by resetting the world in the same save

tools.name: mc_server_action
tools.description: Run a lifecycle action on a server: start, stop, restart (full EC2 reboot) or restart-container (in-place). `start` may return a 402 billing error when the wallet balance is too low.

serverId.description: The target server id (ULID), as returned by mc_list_servers.

tools.name: mc_delete_server

parts.description: Nombre de parts de quotient familial.

revenu_fiscal_reference.description: Revenu fiscal de référence du foyer (€).

situation.description: Situation familiale (seuils célibataire 250 k / couple 500 k).

type_revenu.description: Nature du revenu (ex. rf_location_nue, rcm_dividendes, bic_lmnp).

tools.name: fiscal_surtaxe_pv_immobiliere
tools.description: Surtaxe sur les plus-values immobilières — Taxe additionnelle sur les plus-values immobilières nettes imposables supérieures à 50 000 € (barème par tranches).

tools.name: retraite_ps_pension
tools.description: Prélèvements sociaux sur une pension (brut → net) — CSG (taux 0/3,8/6,6/8,3 % selon le RFR et les parts) + CRDS + CASA + 1 % maladie sur la part de pension complémentaire. Rend la pension nette, la tranche CSG et le taux effectif. Barème 2026 (seuils RFR 2024).

rfr.description: Revenu fiscal de référence 2024 du foyer (€) — détermine la tranche CSG. Si absent, la pension sert de proxy et la tranche est « estimée ».

parts.description: Parts fiscales du foyer (interpolation linéaire des seuils entre 1 et 2 parts).

montant_complementaire.description: Part de la pension relevant d'un régime complémentaire (Agirc-Arrco, Ircantec, CRPN, comp. libéraux…), soumise en plus au 1 % maladie aux tranches médiane/normale. Défaut 0 = base seule.

tools.name: retraite_estimation
tools.description: Estimation de pension (données partielles) — Pension approchée à partir du statut, du revenu, de l'âge et de l'âge de départ : carrière reconstituée, SAM plafonné au PASS, décote. Rend un point central, une fourchette et un niveau de confiance. Ce N'est PAS un calcul certain — il remplace un relevé de carrière (RIS) manquant, pas l'inverse.

statut.description: Statut : "salarié cadre", "salarié non-cadre", "fonctionnaire", "profession libérale"… (mots-clés reconnus, insensible à la casse).

annee_debut_carriere.description: Année de début de carrière — resserre la fourchette si fournie.

trimestres_acquis.description: Trimestres déjà acquis (RIS) — resserre la fourchette si fourni.

traitement_indiciaire.description: Fonctionnaire uniquement : dernier traitement indiciaire brut annuel, hors primes.

tools.name: retraite_pension_regime
tools.description: Pension d'un régime en points (Agirc-Arrco, complémentaires, bases CNAVPL) — Pension brute d'UN régime calculé en points (points × valeur de service 2026 × coefficient). Couvre Agirc-Arrco, Ircantec, RCI, RAFP, les 10 bases CNAVPL libérales et les complémentaires/ASV de caisse (CARMF, CIPAV, CARPIMKO, CARCDSF, CAVEC…). Contrôle de vraisemblance intégré (anti-erreur de sous-régime). Pour un régime en annuités/SAM (CNAV) ou en traitement (fonction publique), utiliser retraite_estimation.

code_regime.description: Code du régime (voir la capacité retraite_regimes pour la liste). Ex. agirc_arrco, carmf_rcv, cipav_base.

points.description: Nombre de points acquis dans ce régime (relevé de carrière / relevé de caisse).

age_depart.description: Âge de liquidation (ans). Défaut = taux plein (pas de décote ni de majoration). Un départ anticipé/reporté applique le coefficient du régime.

age_legal.description: Âge légal du régime (ancre du temps choisi). Défaut 64.

trimestres_manquants.description: Trimestres manquants pour le taux plein — décote sur les régimes qui l'appliquent (complémentaires salariés). Défaut 0.

trimestres_acquis.description: Bases CNAVPL uniquement : trimestres tous régimes acquis (pour le prorata/décote). Défaut 0.

trimestres_requis.description: Bases CNAVPL uniquement : trimestres requis pour le taux plein. Défaut 172.

tools.name: retraite_pension_totale
tools.description: Pension totale consolidée (multi-régimes, le détail du RIS) — Somme les régimes EN POINTS d'un relevé (base CNAVPL + tous les complémentaires/ASV), splitte base/complémentaire, applique la couche brut→net (1 % maladie sur la seule part complémentaire). Le régime de base salarié (CNAV) et la fonction publique ne sont pas en points : les fournir via pensions_fournies (issues de retraite_estimation ou du RIS) pour un total réellement total. Chaque jambe est vraisemblance-vérifiée ; la confiance globale suit la jambe la plus faible.

regimes.description: Régimes en points du relevé. Chaque item : { code_regime, points, [age_depart, age_legal, trimestres_manquants, trimestres_acquis, trimestres_requis] }.

pensions_fournies.description: Jambes NON calculées par nous (ex. CNAV base, fonction publique) : { label, montant_annuel, [etage:"base"|"complementaire"] }. Additionnées telles quelles, flaggées « fourni » (confiance non assertée par le hub).

rfr.description: RFR 2024 du foyer — active le calcul du net (prélèvements sociaux). Sinon le total brut sert de proxy.

inclure_net.description: Calculer la pension nette après prélèvements sociaux (défaut true).

tools.name: retraite_regimes
tools.description: Liste des régimes de retraite calculables par points — Découverte : renvoie les régimes en points calculables via retraite_pension_regime (code, libellé, machine, étage, valeur de service 2026, taux de réversion). Filtrable par famille.

tools.name: retraite_optimisation
tools.description: Optimisation de fin de carrière (menu classé des leviers) — À partir d'une situation (âge, trimestres, SAM, statut, enfants…), renvoie le MENU CLASSÉ des leviers d'optimisation retraite avec gain/ROI/confiance/sources : rachat de trimestres (2 options), surcote parentale, retraite progressive, âge de départ optimal, cumul emploi-retraite, optimisation du SAM, PER fin de carrière. PAS de total sommé (les leviers ne s'additionnent pas naïvement) — chaque levier chiffré séparément, classé par pertinence. Chaque montant porte sa confiance et sa source (Legifrance/BOFiP/service-public).

date_naissance.description: Date de naissance (YYYY-MM-DD) — recale le gel LFSS 2026 et la fenêtre surcote parentale.

sam.description: Salaire annuel moyen (25 meilleures années) — active les gains chiffrés.

trim_manquants.description: Trimestres manquants pour le taux plein — active le levier rachat.

pension_brute_annuelle.description: Pension de base brute annuelle — active les gains nets.

nb_enfants.description: Nombre d'enfants — active surcote parentale (MDA) + majoration ≥3.

mda_parentale.description: ≥1 trimestre de majoration de durée d'assurance pour enfant.

tmi.description: TMI (0-1) — chiffre l'économie d'IR du rachat / PER.

quotite_travail.description: Retraite progressive : quotité de temps partiel (0-1).

salaires_annuels.description: Optionnel : carrière année par année ({annee, salaire_brut}) pour l'optimisation du SAM.

tools.name: retraite_rachat
tools.description: Rachat de trimestres (VPLR — coût, gain, ROI) — Coût et rentabilité d'un rachat de trimestres (versement pour la retraite, art. L351-14-1). Barème 2026 (Circulaire CNAV 2026-04) selon âge/option/revenu, 2 options (taux seul / taux et durée), coût net d'IR (déductible), gain de pension et ROI en années. Gère le rachat d'études (abattement ≤ 40 ans) et de stage (12 % PMSS). Plafond légal 12 trimestres tous motifs.

n_trim.description: Nombre de trimestres à racheter (max 12 tous motifs).

option.description: "taux" (taux seul) ou "taux_duree" (taux et durée). Le stage est taux seul uniquement.

motif.description: Études (abattement ≤ 40 ans), années incomplètes, ou stage (12 % PMSS, ≤ 30 ans, max 2).

revenu_moyen.description: Moyenne des revenus des 3 dernières années (D351-8) — détermine la tranche du barème.

sam.description: SAM (25 meilleures années) — chiffre le gain de pension.

trim_manquants.description: Trimestres manquants pour le taux plein (pilote la décote et le gain).

pension_brute_annuelle.description: Pension brute annuelle — chiffre le gain net.

tools.name: retraite_surcote_parentale
tools.description: Surcote parentale (+1,25 %/trim, max 5 %) — Majoration de pension pour les parents au taux plein un an avant l'âge légal (art. L351-1-2-1). 1,25 % par trimestre travaillé dans la fenêtre [âge légal − 1 an ; âge légal), plafonné à 4 trimestres (5 %). Conditions : âge légal ≥ 63 ans, durée requise atteinte, ≥ 1 trimestre de majoration enfant (MDA). Gère le gel LFSS 2026.

date_naissance.description: Date de naissance (YYYY-MM-DD) — détermine l'âge légal + le gel LFSS 2026.

age_legal.description: Alternative à la date de naissance : âge légal en années.

trimestres_cotises_fenetre.description: Trimestres cotisés dans la fenêtre [âge légal − 1 ; âge légal) — sinon estimé.

pension_brute_annuelle.description: Pension de base brute annuelle — chiffre le gain en €.

tools.name: retraite_progressive
tools.description: Retraite progressive (fraction de pension + temps partiel) — Fraction de pension perçue en travaillant à temps partiel en fin de carrière (art. L161-22-1-5). Continue d'acquérir des droits.

quotite_travail.description: Quotité de temps partiel (0-1). Salarié 0,40-0,80 ; FP 0,50-0,90.

diminution_revenus.description: TNS uniquement : baisse de revenus (0,20-0,60) — alternative à quotite_travail.

pension_brute_annuelle.description: Pension totale brute annuelle (base + comp.) — chiffre la fraction en €.

tools.name: compare_technologies

sites.name: coinranking.com
sites.description: Track live Bitcoin price with Coinranking's Pro Chart. Use advanced drawing tools and technical analysis on this interactive BTC price chart.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_get_view
tools.description: Read what the chart is currently showing: its kind and subject, every option's current value and default, which values can be selected right now (and why the rest can't), the viewer's entitlements, and the shareable URL. Call this first — it grounds every other tool.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_get_stats
tools.description: Summary numbers for every series on the chart — high, low, average, first and last value, with the timestamps of the high and low. Prefer this over reading the whole series for questions like "what is this asset doing", and use it to anchor drawings: these coordinates are exact, where a downsampled series is not.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_get_series
tools.description: The chart's plotted data points as { time, value } pairs in data space — the same coordinates drawings use. Downsampled by default to protect your context; the response says how many points exist and whether it reduced them, and always carries the true high and low so anchoring stays exact. Widen the time period first if you need a range the chart isn't currently showing.

maxPoints.description: Maximum points to return per series (default 100, hard cap 500). Downsampling preserves extremes, and the true high and low are returned separately regardless.

series.description: Dataset keys to include. Omit for every series on the chart.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_list_drawings
tools.description: The shapes currently drawn on the chart, with their points in data space ({ time, value }) rather than pixels. Positions here are directly comparable with what get_series and get_stats return.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_list_history
tools.description: The chart's undo/redo stack, newest first, with a human-readable label for each step. `past` can be undone, `future` can be redone. The stack covers changes since the last navigation, not the whole session.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_list_charts
tools.description: List the charts this viewer has saved, newest first, with each one's uuid, name, kind and subject. No link is returned — pass the kind and subject to navigate to open one. Use it before saving to avoid duplicating a name, or to find a chart the viewer refers to by name.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_configure
tools.description: Change one or more chart options — time period, interval, chart type, log scale, indicators, currency, volume, high/low markers. The whole patch applies as a single undoable step. Values that the viewer can't use are refused with a reason rather than partially applied; call get_view to see what's selectable and why.

options.description: Option keys mapped to their new values. Call get_view first for the valid keys, each option's allowed values, and which are currently selectable. Everything in the patch is applied together as one undoable step, or nothing is.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_navigate
tools.description: Switch to a different chart kind for the current asset, or point the chart at a different asset, category or the global market. A kind switch happens immediately; a subject change returns a URL to open, because it needs a fresh page load. Drawings are discarded on a kind switch, so draw after navigating rather than before.

kind.description: The chart kind to switch to for the current subject — price, market-cap, ranking, and so on. Applied immediately. See get_view for what this chart's subject supports.

id.description: A coin uuid, "global" for the whole market, or "category:<slug>".

slug.description: The coin's slug, when known. Optional.

base.description: A different subject to chart. Returns the destination URL rather than navigating — the caller has to open it.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_history
tools.description: Step backwards or forwards through the chart's change history, or jump straight to an entry by index. This is the same stack the undo/redo buttons drive, and it covers changes since the last navigation rather than the whole session. Call list_history for the entries, their labels and their indices.

action.description: Which way to move through the chart's history.

index.description: Required for `jump`: the entry index from list_history. Ignored otherwise.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_compare
tools.description: Add or remove an overlay plotted alongside this chart — another coin, the global market, or a category. One target per call, each its own undoable step. Targets that can't be plotted here are refused with the reason: the wrong chart kind for that overlay, the chart itself, a duplicate, or the account's overlay limit.

action.description: Whether to start or stop comparing against the target.

target.description: What to compare against: a currency uuid, the literal `global` for the whole market, or `category:<slug>` (e.g. `category:defi`). Call get_view to see what's already being compared.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_draw
tools.description: Draw a line, rectangle, circle or text label on the chart, remove one, or clear them all. Anchors are data coordinates (a timestamp and a value), not screen pixels — call get_stats for exact highs and lows to anchor against. Set the chart's kind and time range BEFORE drawing: switching kind discards annotations, because a shape anchored to price data is meaningless on another scale.

action.description: Add one annotation, remove one by index, or remove all.

points.description: For `add`: anchors in DATA coordinates — `time` is a timestamp and `value` is on the chart's own y-scale, not pixels. A line takes 2 endpoints. A rectangle or circle takes 2 opposite corners, or 4 for an exact quad. A text annotation takes 1 anchor, which becomes the centre of a box sized to the text, or 4 to place the box yourself. Get exact values from get_stats (true highs/lows) or get_series.

text.description: For `add` with type `text`: the label's content.

style.description: For `add`: optional appearance. Defaults to the chart's own drawing style.

fill.description: Body fill for rectangles and circles.

index.description: For `remove`: which annotation, by its position in list_drawings.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_export
tools.description: Export the chart's data as CSV or the chart itself as a PNG image. CSV can be returned directly in the result; saving a file or copying to the clipboard asks the user first, since browsers only allow those during a user gesture.

format.description: `csv` for the underlying data, `png` for a picture of the chart.

destination.description: Where the export goes. `return` (CSV only) hands the text back in this result. `download` saves a file and `clipboard` copies — both prompt the user, because the browser only permits them during a user gesture. Defaults to `return` for CSV and `download` for PNG.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_share_link
tools.description: Get a link that reproduces the chart exactly as it looks now — kind, asset, time range, styling and drawings all travel in the URL. Returns the link by default; set `share` to open the device's share sheet instead, which asks the user first.

share.description: Open the device's share sheet (or copy the link where there isn't one) instead of just returning the URL. Prompts the user, so only set this when they asked to share rather than to see the link.

tools.name: coinranking_prochart_save
tools.description: Save the chart to the viewer's account, save a copy under a new name, rename it, delete it, or discard unsaved edits. Saving needs a name the first time. Deleting asks the viewer to confirm. Call get_view first if you need to know whether the chart is already saved.

action.description: `save` updates the current chart (or creates it, with a name). `save_as` always creates a new one. `rename` retitles it, `delete` removes it, `discard` reverts unsaved edits.

name.description: Required for `save_as` and `rename`, and for `save` when the chart has never been saved. Without it the site would open a naming dialog, which a tool call can't sensibly drive.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

query.description: Search query string.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an update_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Product detail parameters.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart, update line item quantities, or remove items. Batch EVERY change for one request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart once per item. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use line_items[].id from get_cart to update or remove an existing line, passing the ABSOLUTE target quantity (not a delta; quantity 0 removes the line). Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant.

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart. Use to update or remove an existing line. Omit when adding new items.
ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: Quantity. Defaults to 1 for adds and updates. Set to 0 with an existing line id to remove it.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Remove all items from the cart in one step. Use when the user wants to empty their cart or start over.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Proceed to checkout. Verifies the cart is not empty, then MOVES the browser to the checkout page. The tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: manage_orders
tools.description: Navigate to the customer's order history page. Use when the user asks about past orders, order status, tracking, or returns. The user will be prompted to log in if not already authenticated. This MOVES the browser to the order history page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: search_shop_policies_and_faqs
tools.description: Used to get facts about the store's policies, FAQ, or contact details. When the question is about specific policy kinds, set policy_types to those kinds; leave it unset for general FAQ questions. Some examples of questions you can ask are: - What is your return policy? (policy_types: ["refund"]) - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"]) - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"]) - What are your hours of operation? (policy_types: ["contact"]) - Do you offer gift wrapping? (general FAQ, no specific policy kind — leave policy_types unset)

query.description: A natural language query. Searches FAQ pages and articles, and routes policies by keyword when policy_types is omitted.

policy_types.description: Policy kinds to fetch, chosen from the user's question — e.g. ["refund"] for returns/exchanges, ["contact"] for phone/hours/address. Include every kind the question touches. Omit when no specific policy is relevant (e.g. a general FAQ question).

tools.name: quokkapix.apply_recipe

tools.name: quokkapix.apply_settings

tools.name: quokkapix.set_unlock_token

tools.name: quokkapix.start

query.description: The merchant's product, pricing, setup, or feature question.
